messages.author: 755f9cca67993013
messages.subject: Coding F2 natural populations
parts:
Hi all,
Very sorry for my previous meaningless post.

I am working with semi-natural population. I don't have any knowledge of F0 but, all my markers are heterozygous (AB) in F1. I genotyped F2, I got hetereozygous (AB) and homozygous (AA, BB); it means, homozygous ones are recombinants. Now, my issue is how to code these?

I appreciate any kind of help!

Thanks
Ramesh

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Coding F2 natural populations
parts:
It's a bit complicated to deal, in R/qtl, with an F2 with progenitors that are heterozygous.

You first need to determine phase (in other words, the haplotypes) in the F1 parents.
Think of the F1 parents as AB x CD, then you need to convert the genotypes to 14 possible genotype codes, as follows:

1 = AC
2 = BC
3 = AD
4 = BD
5 = A = AC or AD
6 = B = BC or BD
7 = C = AC or BC
8 = D = AD or BD
9 = AC or BD
10 = AD or BC
11 = not AC
12 = not BC
13 = not AD
14 = not BD

For example, if a SNP were segregating in the first F1 parent but not the second, with the phase ab x aa, then the F2 offspring would be aa and ba, and the codes would be

aa = AC or AD = 5
ab = BC or BD = 6

If the phase were instead ba x aa, then the codes for the F2 offspring would be

aa = BC or BD = 6
ab = AC or AD = 5

karl

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Coding F2 natural populations
parts:
You need to figure out phase for those markers...there are four possible:

AB x AB (offspring AA -> 1, AB -> 10, BB -> 4)
AB x BA (offspring AA -> 3, AB -> 9, BB -> 2)
BA x AB (offspring AA -> 2, AB -> 9, BB -> 3)
BA x BA (offspring AA -> 4, AB -> 10, BB -> 1)

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Coding F2 natural populations
parts: > Yes, this makes sense. To make it clear, both the F1 parents are clonally propagated and inbred, there is a possibility of only one phase - AB x AB, am I right?
I wouldn't think so. I thought you'd said that the progenitors were heterozygous rather than inbred lines.
> My second question is, coding 1, 2, 3 is possible in R/qtl?

If the F1 parents have phase AB x AB at all markers, then yes you could code this like a standard intercross formed from inbred lines.

karl
